title: GlacierNet: Glacier outline segmentation from multispectral satellite imagery (synthetic)

sections.abstract: We study glacier outline segmentation from multispectral satellite imagery. We introduce GlacierNet, a convolutional encoder-decoder with a boundary-aware loss.
sections.methods: We train GlacierNet on the AlpineSat-12k dataset using a boundary-aware loss and random tile cropping. All models are trained with a fixed random seed and evaluated on a held-out test split.
sections.results: On AlpineSat-12k, GlacierNet achieves IoU of 0.81, compared with 0.74 for U-Net. Removing the boundary-aware loss lowers IoU in ablation studies. Results are averaged over five runs.
sections.limitations: A key limitation of GlacierNet is that cloud cover above 40% in a tile degrades outlines. Addressing this is left to future work.

sections.abstract: We study fast protein loop modeling. We introduce PolyFold-Lite, a lightweight diffusion model over backbone torsion angles.
sections.methods: We train PolyFold-Lite on the LoopBench dataset using torsion-angle noise scheduling. All models are trained with a fixed random seed and evaluated on a held-out test split.
sections.results: On LoopBench, PolyFold-Lite achieves RMSD of 1.9 Å, compared with 2.6 Å for Rosetta KIC. Removing the torsion noise schedule lowers RMSD in ablation studies. Results are averaged over five runs.
sections.limitations: A key limitation of PolyFold-Lite is that loops longer than 20 residues are modeled poorly. Addressing this is left to future work.

title: CardioTrace: Arrhythmia detection from single-lead ecg (synthetic)

sections.abstract: We study arrhythmia detection from single-lead ECG. We introduce CardioTrace, a one-dimensional residual network with attention pooling.
sections.methods: We train CardioTrace on the HeartWave-5 dataset using attention pooling over beat windows. All models are trained with a fixed random seed and evaluated on a held-out test split.
sections.results: On HeartWave-5, CardioTrace achieves macro F1 of 0.93, compared with 0.88 for ResNet-18. Removing attention pooling lowers macro F1 in ablation studies. Results are averaged over five runs.
sections.limitations: A key limitation of CardioTrace is that all recordings come from a single hospital. Addressing this is left to future work.

title: SoilSense: Soil organic carbon prediction from spectra (synthetic)

sections.abstract: We study soil organic carbon prediction from spectra. We introduce SoilSense, a partial-least-squares model with learned spectral preprocessing.
sections.methods: We train SoilSense on the SoilSpec-Europe dataset using learned Savitzky-Golay preprocessing. All models are trained with a fixed random seed and evaluated on a held-out test split.
sections.results: On SoilSpec-Europe, SoilSense achieves R2 of 0.87, compared with 0.79 for PLSR. Removing learned preprocessing lowers R2 in ablation studies. Results are averaged over five runs.
sections.limitations: A key limitation of SoilSense is that only lab-dried samples were measured. Addressing this is left to future work.

sections.abstract: We study small-sample tabular classification. We introduce KernelTab, a learned-kernel support vector classifier.
sections.methods: We train KernelTab on the TabSmall-40 dataset using marginal-likelihood kernel tuning. All models are trained with a fixed random seed and evaluated on a held-out test split.
sections.results: On TabSmall-40, KernelTab achieves accuracy of 0.76, compared with 0.71 for gradient boosting. Removing kernel tuning lowers accuracy in ablation studies. Results are averaged over five runs.
sections.limitations: A key limitation of KernelTab is that training cost grows cubically with sample count. Addressing this is left to future work.

title: ReefWatch: Coral bleaching detection in drone video (synthetic)

sections.abstract: We study coral bleaching detection in drone video. We introduce ReefWatch, a temporal detector with optical-flow stabilization.
sections.methods: We train ReefWatch on the ReefDrone-3k dataset using optical-flow stabilization of frames. All models are trained with a fixed random seed and evaluated on a held-out test split.
sections.results: On ReefDrone-3k, ReefWatch achieves mAP of 0.69, compared with 0.61 for YOLOv8. Removing optical-flow stabilization lowers mAP in ablation studies. Results are averaged over five runs.
sections.limitations: A key limitation of ReefWatch is that turbid water reduces detection quality. Addressing this is left to future work.

sections.abstract: We study single-step retrosynthesis prediction. We introduce SynthPlan, a template-free transformer with reaction-class conditioning.
sections.methods: We train SynthPlan on the USPTO-Mini dataset using reaction-class conditioning. All models are trained with a fixed random seed and evaluated on a held-out test split.
sections.results: On USPTO-Mini, SynthPlan achieves top-1 accuracy of 52.4%, compared with 47.1% for RetroTemplate. Removing reaction-class conditioning lowers top-1 accuracy in ablation studies. Results are averaged over five runs.
sections.limitations: A key limitation of SynthPlan is that stereochemistry is often predicted incorrectly. Addressing this is left to future work.

sections.abstract: We study wind gust nowcasting. We introduce GustCast, a convolutional LSTM over radar and station data.
sections.methods: We train GustCast on the GustArchive-DE dataset using radar-station fusion. All models are trained with a fixed random seed and evaluated on a held-out test split.
sections.results: On GustArchive-DE, GustCast achieves MAE of 1.4 m/s, compared with 2.0 m/s for persistence forecasting. Removing radar-station fusion lowers MAE in ablation studies. Results are averaged over five runs.
sections.limitations: A key limitation of GustCast is that forecasts degrade in complex terrain. Addressing this is left to future work.
